title: Implement 'super' keyword in AppScript parser and interpreter
description: Implement 'super' as a valid receiver in message-send expressions. Parser must recognise 'super' as a special receiver token (distinct from an identifier). Interpreter must dispatch the message using the superclass of the current method's class, not the dynamic type of self — matching Objective-C semantics. Must include AGPL licence headers, nullability annotations, NS_DESIGNATED_INITIALIZER/NS_UNAVAILABLE where applicable, and pass Clang static analyser.

title: Verify all tests pass for 'super' feature
description: Run the full unit test suite (AppScriptTests) and the AppScriptHarness integration tests after implementing 'super'. Fix any failures. Confirm static analyser reports zero warnings. Ensure the harness exits 0.

title: Unit tests: 'super' message dispatch in interpreter
description: Write XCTest unit tests for the interpreter covering 'super' keyword behaviour: parsing 'super' as a receiver, dispatching a message to the superclass, verifying that 'super' in a class method dispatches to the superclass class method, and that 'super' outside a class definition is an error. Tests must follow naming convention test_<method>_<scenario>_<outcome>.

title: Harness test: 'super' message send end-to-end
description: Add an AppScriptHarness integration test script (Super.appscript + Super.expected) that exercises 'super' through the full parse-interpret pipeline. Must define a class hierarchy where a subclass calls [super init] or another superclass method and the result is compared to the .expected file.

title: Design: add 'super' keyword to AppScript language
description: AppScript needs to support sending messages to the superclass via 'super', e.g. 'self = [super init]'. Document the design in ARCHITECTURE.md: how 'super' is parsed, how it is distinguished from 'self', and how the runtime dispatches to the superclass method implementation. Must follow CODING_STANDARDS.md.
close_reason: Design documented in ARCHITECTURE.md: super dispatch semantics, self reassignment, block restriction, category behaviour, parse error cases.

title: Extend AppScript for Cocoa Prototyping
description: Implement unary minus, logical operators, and function/constant access using intentionally designed object-oriented interface approach
close_reason: All subtasks complete: unary minus, logical operators, BridgeSupport parser, function wrapping, and constant/enum access. ARCHITECTURE.md and DocC updated throughout.

title: Add macOS UI to AppScriptHarness for displaying test results
description: Currently the harness runs headlessly and exits. It needs a proper macOS window with a table view showing each test name, pass/fail status, expected output, and actual output. Include a Run button and a summary line (N passed, M failed). This replaces the current fprintf/exit approach with a persistent UI suitable for interactive development.
close_reason: Implemented ASTestResult model, ASHarnessWindowController with programmatic NSTableView (status/test/expected/actual columns), Run button, summary label. AppDelegate updated to show window and auto-run on launch.

title: Xcode project setup: AppScript framework, AppScriptTests, and AppScriptHarness targets
description: Set up the Xcode project with three targets as specified in CODING_STANDARDS.md: AppScript (dynamic framework), AppScriptTests (XCTest unit test bundle), and AppScriptHarness (macOS application). Create the directory structure: AppScript/, AppScriptTests/, AppScriptHarness/, AppScriptHarness/Scripts/, LICENSES/. Add the AGPL-3.0-or-later license header to every source file. Configure ASan and TSan build configurations for CI. This task must be completed before any other implementation work begins.

title: Callable uncaught exception handler with augmented backtrace
description: Add a public API function ASInstallUncaughtExceptionHandler() that installs an NSUncaughtExceptionHandler which, for ASRuntimeErrorException exceptions, replaces the default Cocoa backtrace report with the hybrid backtrace from ASErrorHybridCallStackKey. The framework must not install this automatically. Update AppScriptHarness to call the installer at launch. Depends on appscript-oot hybrid backtrace.

title: AppScript call stack backtrace with receiver and parameter values
description: When reportError:node:context: fires, print a full AppScript-level call stack showing each method frame with its receiver (-description), parameter names and argument values, script path, and call-site line number. Requires a thread-local frame stack on ASInterpreter: push an ASCallFrame in evaluateMethodBody: and executeBlockBody:, pop on normal return, walk and print on error. No public API changes needed.

title: Source context display at AppScript error (clang-style)
description: Read the .appscript source file at error time, extract the error line, and print it with a caret (^) under the column — matching the clang/rustc diagnostic style. scriptPath and line/column are always available in ASExecutionContext. Must handle missing file gracefully.
close_reason: Implemented ASSourceContext helper in ASInterpreter.m: reads source file via NSURL+AppScriptFileReading, tab-expands line, appends caret at correct column. 7 unit tests covering all 5 requirements. All unit/sanitizer/integration tests pass.

title: Hybrid spliced AppScript+ObjC backtrace
description: Combine [NSThread callStackSymbols] with the AppScript thread-local frame stack to produce a single interleaved trace. Filter out known AppScript runtime frames (ASForwardInvocationIMP, evaluateMethodBody:, evaluateMessageSend:context:, executeStatement:context:, etc.) by substring matching and replace each cluster with the corresponding AppScript call frame. Native ObjC frames pass through verbatim. Depends on the thread-local call stack from the AppScript backtrace feature.
close_reason: Implemented hybrid spliced AppScript+ObjC backtrace; all tests pass

title: Local variable dump at AppScript error site
description: At the point where reportError:node:context: fires, enumerate all bindings visible in the current scope chain and print them alongside the error. ASScope already supports valueForName:/hasName:; needs a new method to enumerate all visible bindings. Low effort, high value.
close_reason: Implemented: allVisibleBindings on ASScope, ASErrorLocalsKey in ASInterpreter, 5 new tests. All unit (default/ASan/TSan) and integration tests pass.

title: Add GNUmakefile for AppScriptHarness app (GNUstep)
description: Create a GNUmakefile in AppScript/AppScriptHarness/ to build the AppScriptHarness tool as a GNUstep application or command-line tool. The harness (main.m, ASTestRunner) links against the AppScript framework. This is the runner used for integration tests and manual script execution.
close_reason: Added AppScriptHarness application target to GNUmakefile: application.make, per-target NEEDS_GUI, RESOURCE_FILES for scripts

title: Port unit tests to GNUstep XCTest
description: Create a GNUmakefile for AppScript/AppScriptTests/ to build and run the unit tests using GNUstep's XCTest (https://github.com/gnustep/tools-xctest). All existing test files (ASASTNodeTests, ASBoxerTests, ASBridgeSupportParserTests, ASInterpreterTests, ASLexerTests, ASLoaderTests, ASParserTests, NSNumber/NSString/NSURL/NSObject/NSBundle tests, etc.) should be included. Note: AppScriptHarnessUITests (XCUIAutomation integration tests) are excluded as GNUstep XCTest does not support XCUIAutomation.

title: Add GNUmakefile for AppScript framework (GNUstep)
description: Create a GNUmakefile in AppScript/AppScript/ to build the AppScript framework as a GNUstep library. The framework contains the lexer, parser, interpreter, AST nodes, boxing, bridge support, and runtime installer. All .m files in AppScript/AppScript/ should be compiled. The output should be a shared library (framework equivalent) suitable for linking by the harness and tests.
close_reason: GNUmakefile created at AppScript/GNUmakefile; builds AppScript.framework with all 41 sources using framework.make and -fobjc-arc

title: Support loading scripts from arbitrary paths and runtime strings
description: Add an API to load AppScript scripts from arbitrary file paths (not just bundled resources) and from NSString/source supplied at runtime. Scripts loaded this way should participate fully in the AppScript runtime: they can define new classes, extend existing AppScript classes with new methods/properties, or replace existing class definitions. This mirrors the flexibility of embedded scripting engines (e.g. JSContext eval, Lua dostring) and enables use cases like user-defined scripts, plugin systems, and REPL-style development workflows.
close_reason: All correctness defects fixed: ASLoaderErrorFileNotFound now returned for missing files, duplicate detection is atomic (TOCTOU race closed), NSNull removed from NSUnderlyingErrorKey, and tests tightened to verify error codes and concurrent behavior.

title: Migrate applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed: to AppScript
description: Once appscript-7u5 is done, the AppDelegate.m stub can have applicationShouldTerminateAfterLastWindowClosed: removed. Move it to AppDelegate.appscript as a category method returning YES. This removes the last Objective-C method from AppDelegate.m that exists purely because of primitive return-type limitations. AppDelegate.m keeps the @implementation stub and windowController property extension since those still need ObjC.

title: Use protocol type encoding for sentinel IMP registration
description: installSentinelForMethodNode:onClass: and the category path both use ASTypeEncodingForParamCount (all-id encoding) when calling class_addMethod/class_replaceMethod. If the selector is declared in a protocol adopted by the class (or its superclasses), the sentinel should use the protocol's type encoding instead. This allows AppScript methods implementing protocol methods with primitive return types (e.g. BOOL) to be installed with the correct ObjC type encoding. Implementation: (1) extract ASProtocolTypeEncodingForSelector (const char * variant) from ASProtocolMethodSignatureForSelector, (2) use it in both installSentinelForMethodNode:onClass: and the category install path, (3) update ARCHITECTURE.md to document this behaviour, (4) add unit tests. Per CODING_STANDARDS the ARCHITECTURE.md update must be in the same commit as the code change.

title: Expose NSClassFromString to AppScript
description: AppDelegate needs to look up a class by name at runtime (NSClassFromString). This is a C function unavailable in AppScript. Once the '#' type encoding bug is fixed in ASBoxer, add NSClassFromString to Foundation BridgeSupport so AppScript can call [ASFoundation NSClassFromString: name]. Alternatively, add a category method -[NSString as_class] that calls NSClassFromString and returns id.
close_reason: Implemented and all unit tests pass; committed in 6d22063

title: Add out-parameter-free file-reading API
description: AppScript cannot call methods with NSError** out-parameters (e.g. [NSString stringWithContentsOfURL:encoding:error:]). ASTestRunner needs to read .expected files. Add a category method such as +[NSString as_stringWithContentsOfURL:encoding:] that reads the file and returns nil on error, so AppScript code can call it without an error out-parameter.
close_reason: Implemented and all unit tests pass; committed in 6d22063

title: Fix ASBoxer: handle '#' (Class) type encoding
description: ASBoxer.m's ASBoxBytes function has no case for '#' (the ObjC type encoding for Class). It falls through to the default NSValue wrapping, so any message-send that returns a Class (e.g. [obj class], NSClassFromString) returns an NSValue instead of the Class object. The fix is to add a '#' case that reads the Class pointer and returns it as id, matching the '@' case.
close_reason: Implemented and all unit tests pass; committed in 6d22063

title: Implement automatic function wrapping via BridgeSupport
description: Using the BridgeSupport parser output, dynamically register C functions as Objective-C message sends at runtime. Each wrapped function should box all id arguments to the appropriate C types before calling, and box the C return value back to id. Follow the design documented in ARCHITECTURE.md (updated in the design task). Follow CODING_STANDARDS.md: AGPL header, unit tests, documentation comments, harness tests for representative wrapped functions.
close_reason: ASBridgeSupportInstaller dynamically wraps C functions as class methods on AS<Framework> proxy classes. NSBundle+AppScriptBridgeSupportLoading provides host-app entry point. All unit tests and 25/25 harness scripts pass.

title: Implement constant access via BridgeSupport
description: Using the BridgeSupport parser output, expose C constants (numeric, string, enum values) as class methods so AppScript code can access them as message sends. The approach should be determined by the design task (appscript-a4t). All values must be boxed to id. Follow CODING_STANDARDS.md: AGPL header, unit tests, documentation comments. Update ARCHITECTURE.md if implementation details diverge from the design. Add a harness test exercising several representative constants.
close_reason: Constants (via dlsym) and enumerations (from XML values) installed as direct IMP blocks on the proxy class. Fixed fixture: NSNotFound is an enum (value64='-1') matching real Foundation.bridgesupport; M_PI replaced with NSFoundationVersionNumber. 26/26 harness scripts pass.

title: Design and document BridgeSupport integration in ARCHITECTURE.md
description: Research Apple's BridgeSupport XML metadata format and design how the AppScript runtime will use it to automatically expose C functions and constants. Decide how functions become message sends (e.g. class methods on a generated wrapper class, or instance methods on NSNumber for math functions) and how constants become accessible (e.g. class methods). Update ARCHITECTURE.md with a new 'BridgeSupport integration' section describing the loading mechanism, the boxing/unboxing rules for function arguments and return values, and how constants are addressed in AppScript code. No implementation in this task — design and document only.
close_reason: Implemented and all unit + integration tests pass

title: Implement BridgeSupport XML parser
description: Implement a parser that reads Apple BridgeSupport XML files (located in /System/Library/BridgeSupport/) and extracts function signatures, constant names/types, and enum values. The parser output should be an in-memory representation (Objective-C classes) consumed by the function-wrapping and constant-access tasks. Follow CODING_STANDARDS.md: AGPL header, unit tests for every public method, documentation comments. Update ARCHITECTURE.md to reflect any implementation details that differ from the design.
close_reason: BridgeSupport XML parser fully implemented with 18 unit tests and integration test passing (24/24 harness scripts pass)

title: Implement negated method on NSNumber for unary minus
description: Add a `negated` method to the NSNumber arithmetic category so AppScript code can negate a number via a message send (e.g. `[n negated]`) rather than a C unary minus operator. Update ARCHITECTURE.md to document this method alongside the existing arithmetic category. Follow all guidelines in CODING_STANDARDS.md: AGPL header, unit tests, public method documentation comment, and a harness test.
close_reason: Implemented and all unit + integration tests pass

title: Implement and: or: not logical operator methods on NSNumber
description: Add `and:`, `or:`, and `not` methods to NSNumber (in a new AppScriptLogic category) so AppScript code can express logical operations as message sends. These return an NSNumber BOOL. Update ARCHITECTURE.md to document this new category alongside the control-flow categories. Follow all guidelines in CODING_STANDARDS.md: AGPL header, unit tests for each method, public method documentation comment, and a harness test.
close_reason: Implemented and all unit + integration tests pass

title: Support unary - for negative number literals
description: AppScript currently cannot express negative number literals. A developer writing -3.14 gets a parse error because the minus token is consumed as punctuation and not followed by a method declaration. The fix is to handle a leading minus token in the parser's parseExpression method when it is immediately followed by a number literal token, folding the sign into the ASNumberLiteralNode value. Also update ARCHITECTURE.md to document the syntax, add unit tests for parser and lexer, and add a harness script NegativeNumbers.appscript.

title: Harness test: return value from method (explicit nil return)
description: Add ReturnValues.as and ReturnValues.expected. Verify that: a method with an explicit return statement returns the expected value, a method that returns self enables message chaining, a method that returns nil propagates nil correctly. This covers the ARCHITECTURE.md guidance that methods returning 'void' should return self, and nil indicates the absence of an object.

title: Harness test: multi-class interaction
description: Add MultiClass.as and MultiClass.expected. Define two AppScript classes in the same script file where one class's method creates and uses an instance of the other. This exercises the full parse→install→invoke pipeline across multiple class definitions and verifies inter-class message sends work correctly end-to-end.

title: Harness test: _cmd implicit variable in methods
description: Add ImplicitVars.as and ImplicitVars.expected. Verify that both self and _cmd are implicitly in scope inside instance and class method bodies as specified in ARCHITECTURE.md. Use _cmd (the current selector as a string) and self in a method body and return a result that confirms their values match expectations.

title: Harness test: complete arithmetic operations
description: Extend or replace Arithmetic.as/Arithmetic.expected to cover all four arithmetic operations: numberByAdding:, numberBySubtracting:, numberByMultiplyingBy:, numberByDividingBy:. The existing script only tests addition. The new script should exercise all four and return a combined result whose -description matches the expected file.

title: Harness test: do:while: loop
description: Add DoWhile.as and DoWhile.expected. Exercise NSObject's -do:while: runtime method: write a loop that accumulates a result over several iterations, verifying the body block runs while the condition block returns a truthy value and stops when it returns nil or NO. Verify the loop does not run if the condition is false on first test (as per ARCHITECTURE.md).

title: Harness test: do:until: loop (collection enumeration pattern)
description: Add DoUntil.as and DoUntil.expected. Exercise NSObject's -do:until: method using the NSEnumerator pattern shown in ARCHITECTURE.md: create an enumerator, use do:while: with nextObject to iterate through all elements, verify results. Also exercise -do:until: directly to confirm the body runs at least once even when condition is immediately false.

title: Harness test: ifTrue:ifFalse: conditional control flow
description: Add ConditionalFlow.as and ConditionalFlow.expected. Exercise NSNumber's -ifTrue:ifFalse: runtime method: call it with YES to verify the true branch executes and returns its value, call it with NO to verify the false branch executes. Verify the return value of the branch is propagated as the result of the expression.

title: Harness test: method override and inheritance
description: Add Inheritance.as and Inheritance.expected. Define a base AppScript class and a subclass that overrides a method. Verify the subclass's override is invoked, and that the subclass can access properties/methods defined in the base class. This exercises method_setImplementation-based override installation per ARCHITECTURE.md.

title: Harness test: class and instance methods
description: Add ClassMethods.as and ClassMethods.expected. Define a class with at least one + class method and one - instance method. Exercise calling the class method to create an instance, then sending an instance method. Verify correct dispatch and return values for both method types.

title: Harness test: class definition with properties
description: Add ClassProperties.as and ClassProperties.expected. Define an AppScript class with @property declarations using various modifiers: default (strong, nonatomic), readonly, copy. Verify that the synthesised KVC-compliant accessor methods work correctly: setter writes and getter reads the correct value; readonly property has no setter; copy property stores a copy.

title: Harness test: categories on Objective-C classes
description: Add Categories.as and Categories.expected. Define a @category on an existing Objective-C class (e.g. NSString or NSObject). Add a new method via the category. Verify that instances of that Objective-C class respond to the added method and return the expected result. Exercises the @category keyword and runtime category installation.

title: Harness test: self inside blocks refers to enclosing method receiver
description: Add BlockSelf.as and BlockSelf.expected. Define a class with an instance method that creates a block; inside the block, send a message to self and verify self is the enclosing receiver, not the block itself. This exercises the ARCHITECTURE.md rule that self inside a block always refers to the enclosing method's receiver.

title: Harness test: blocks with no arguments
description: Add BlocksNoArgs.as and BlocksNoArgs.expected. Exercise: declare a block literal with no arguments using ^{ ... } syntax, call the block using the block variable, verify the block executes and its return value is accessible.

title: Harness test: blocks with arguments
description: Add BlocksWithArgs.as and BlocksWithArgs.expected. Exercise: declare a block using ^(arg1) { ... } and ^(arg1 arg2) { ... } syntax (bare identifier parameters), invoke the block with arguments, verify correct argument binding and return value.

title: Harness test: unary and keyword message sends
description: Add MessageSends.as and MessageSends.expected. Exercise: unary message send (e.g. [str length]), keyword message send (e.g. [str stringByAppendingString:]), multi-keyword message send (e.g. [str writeToFile:atomically:]). Include both messages to AppScript objects and to Objective-C objects requiring auto-boxing of arguments and unboxing of return values.

title: Harness test: block variable capture from enclosing scope
description: Add BlockCapture.as and BlockCapture.expected. Exercise: a block that captures a variable from the enclosing method scope by name, verifies the captured value is accessible inside the block. Also exercise that a non-constant captured variable is mutable from inside the block (implicit __block semantics per ARCHITECTURE.md). Verify it is an error to declare a local variable in the block with the same name as a captured variable (test only the success cases).

title: Harness test: array literals
description: Add ArrayLiterals.as and ArrayLiterals.expected. Exercise: @[...] array literal declaration with multiple elements, sending messages to the resulting NSArray (count, objectAtIndex:). Return a result whose -description matches the expected file.

title: Harness test: dictionary literals
description: Add DictionaryLiterals.as and DictionaryLiterals.expected. Exercise: @{key: value, ...} dictionary literal, objectForKey:, count. Return a result whose -description matches the expected file.

title: Harness test: number and boolean literals
description: Add NumberLiterals.as and NumberLiterals.expected. Exercise: integer literal boxing (id n = 42), float literal boxing (id pi = 3.14), YES boxing, NO boxing. Use -description on the results to produce a known string. Verify auto-boxing produces NSNumber instances with correct values.

title: Harness test: string literals
description: Add StringLiterals.as and StringLiterals.expected. Exercise: @"..." string literal assignment, sending messages to string literals (e.g. uppercaseString), string comparison. Return a string whose -description matches the expected file.

title: Harness test: variable declarations (id, weak id, constant id)
description: Add Variables.as and Variables.expected to AppScriptHarness/Scripts/. The script must exercise: plain id variable declaration, weak id variable declaration, constant id declaration (verify it holds value), and attempting to reassign a constant must crash (test only the success cases in the harness). Return a string summarising the values so the expected file can verify them. Follow CODING_STANDARDS.md harness test structure.

title: ObjC runtime integration: register AppScript classes and install method IMPs
description: Implement ASRuntimeInstaller in AppScript/ASRuntimeInstaller.h and AppScript/ASRuntimeInstaller.m. Given a parsed set of class/category definitions: register new class pairs with objc_allocateClassPair / objc_registerClassPair using the declared superclass. For each method in the class, create a trampoline IMP that (a) boxes incoming C parameters to id using ASBoxer, (b) invokes ASInterpreter with the method's AST fragment, (c) unboxes the return value using ASBoxer. Use class_addMethod for new methods and method_setImplementation for overrides. Synthesize KVC-compliant getter (and setter unless readonly) for each @property not marked dynamic, unless the developer provides a custom implementation. For @category definitions, add/replace methods on the existing class. On interpreter error, output the AppScript file path and line number to stderr then call abort(). All public methods need /// DocC comments. Create ASRuntimeInstallerTests.m.

title: NSBundle+AppScriptLoading: loadAppScriptsInBundle: category
description: Implement NSBundle+AppScriptLoading in AppScript/NSBundle+AppScriptLoading.h and AppScript/NSBundle+AppScriptLoading.m. The category method - (BOOL)loadAppScriptsInBundle:(NSError **)error must: (1) track which bundles have been loaded and return NO with an error if called twice on the same bundle, (2) search for *.as files in the bundle using NSBundle's resource methods, (3) for each file, read the source, run ASLexer then ASParser, abort with error on parse failure, (4) pass the resulting AST to ASRuntimeInstaller to register classes and install methods. The method must be thread-safe. All public methods need /// DocC comments. Create NSBundle+AppScriptLoadingTests.m. Also write a DocC article AppScript/Documentation.docc/LoadingAndRunningAppScriptFiles.md covering the full load->parse->install->invoke pipeline, linked from the framework catalog.

title: NSNumber+AppScriptArithmetic: arithmetic category methods
description: Implement NSNumber+AppScriptArithmetic in AppScript/NSNumber+AppScriptArithmetic.h and AppScript/NSNumber+AppScriptArithmetic.m. Add four methods to NSNumber: - (NSNumber *)numberByAdding:(NSNumber *)other, - (NSNumber *)numberBySubtracting:(NSNumber *)other, - (NSNumber *)numberByMultiplyingBy:(NSNumber *)other, - (NSNumber *)numberByDividingBy:(NSNumber *)other. These must use double arithmetic and return NSNumber instances. All methods need /// DocC comments. Create NSNumber+AppScriptArithmeticTests.m with unit tests for each operation including edge cases (zero, negative numbers, large values).

title: AppScriptHarness: integration test harness application
description: Implement the AppScriptHarness macOS application as specified in CODING_STANDARDS.md. The harness must: (1) call loadAppScriptsInBundle: on a bundle containing *.as test scripts, (2) for each script, find the class whose name ends in Test, instantiate it, and call -runTests, (3) call -description on the returned object and compare to the content of the paired *.expected file, (4) print a pass/fail summary to stdout, (5) exit with code 0 if all pass or 1 if any fail. The harness must run headlessly for CI. Add at least one end-to-end harness test script (e.g. ArithmeticTest.as with ArithmeticTest.expected) that exercises the full load->parse->interpret->result pipeline. All source files need the AGPL license header.

title: NSNumber+AppScriptControlFlow and NSObject+AppScriptControlFlow categories
description: Implement control flow categories. NSNumber+AppScriptControlFlow in AppScript/NSNumber+AppScriptControlFlow.h/.m: add - (id)ifTrue:(id (^)(void))trueBlock ifFalse:(id (^)(void))falseBlock — executes trueBlock if the receiver is non-zero and non-nil, falseBlock otherwise; returns the result of whichever block executed, or nil if the block has no return value. NSObject+AppScriptControlFlow in AppScript/NSObject+AppScriptControlFlow.h/.m: add - (id)do:(id (^)(void))aBlock while:(id (^)(void))testBlock (runs aBlock while testBlock returns non-nil/non-NO, may not run aBlock at all) and - (id)do:(id (^)(void))aBlock until:(id (^)(void))testBlock (runs aBlock until testBlock returns nil or NO, guaranteed to run at least once). All methods need /// DocC comments. Create corresponding test files.

title: ASParser: parse AppScript token stream into an AST
description: Implement ASParser in AppScript/ASParser.h and AppScript/ASParser.m. The parser consumes the token stream produced by ASLexer and produces an array of top-level AST nodes (class and category definitions). Parse all language constructs per ARCHITECTURE.md: @class declarations with superclass and optional protocol list, @category declarations, @property declarations with optional modifiers, instance and class method definitions with infix selector syntax, variable declarations (id, weak id, constant id), message sends (including multi-keyword selectors), block literals (^{ } and ^(args) { }), return statements, string/number/array/dictionary/nil/bool/selector literals. The parser must produce actionable error messages with line numbers for syntax errors. All public methods need /// DocC comments. Create ASParserTests.m with comprehensive unit tests.

title: ASLexer: tokenize AppScript source into a token stream
description: Implement ASLexer in AppScript/ASLexer.h and AppScript/ASLexer.m. The lexer must tokenize all AppScript language constructs: identifiers, keywords (@class, @end, @category, @property, id, weak, constant, return, self, _cmd), number literals (integer and float), string literals (@"..."), array literals (@[...]), dictionary literals (@{...}), boolean literals (YES, NO), the nil literal, block introducers (^), brackets ([ ] { } ( )), the colon separator, class/instance method markers (+ -), operators, and comments (//).  All public methods must have /// DocC documentation comments in the header. Create ASLexerTests.m with XCTest unit tests following the naming convention test_<method>_<scenario>_<outcome>. Tests must cover each token type, whitespace handling, comment stripping, and error cases (e.g. unterminated string literals).

title: ASBoxer: automatic boxing and unboxing of ObjC primitive types
description: Implement ASBoxer in AppScript/ASBoxer.h and AppScript/ASBoxer.m. Boxing: convert C primitives (int, NSInteger, CGFloat, double, float, BOOL, etc.) and C strings to appropriate NSNumber/NSString/NSValue instances. Unboxing: inspect a method's actual ObjC type encoding (via NSMethodSignature) and convert NSObject arguments to the required C type by sending the appropriate NSValue/NSNumber accessor (e.g. integerValue, doubleValue, boolValue). Handle return value boxing: wrap primitive return values into NSNumber or NSString. Handle void return. Handle struct types via NSValue. All public methods need /// DocC comments. Create ASBoxerTests.m with unit tests for each supported type conversion in both directions.

title: ASInterpreter: evaluate AppScript AST nodes
description: Implement ASInterpreter in AppScript/ASInterpreter.h and AppScript/ASInterpreter.m. The interpreter must: maintain a variable scope stack (push/push scope on method/block entry, pop on exit), resolve identifiers against the scope stack, evaluate all expression node types (message sends, block literals, literals), implement variable declaration with weak/constant semantics, implement assignment with constant-reassignment error detection, evaluate multi-keyword message sends, implement return value semantics for methods and blocks, make self and _cmd implicitly available in method bodies, implement block capture semantics (captured variables from enclosing AppScript scope are automatically __block-equivalent for non-constant variables), ensure self inside a block refers to the enclosing method's receiver. The interpreter must be thread-safe: multiple threads may invoke it simultaneously. Document the owning dispatch queue for all mutable state. All public methods need /// DocC comments. Create ASInterpreterTests.m.

title: AST node classes for all AppScript language constructs
description: Define AST node classes in AppScript/. Each construct needs its own class: ASClassDefinitionNode (class name, superclass name, protocol names, properties, methods), ASCategoryDefinitionNode (class name, category name, methods), ASPropertyNode (name, modifiers), ASMethodNode (selector, parameter names, body statements, isClassMethod), ASVariableDeclarationNode (name, initializer expression, isWeak, isConstant), ASAssignmentNode, ASMessageSendNode (receiver, selector parts, arguments), ASBlockLiteralNode (parameter names, body statements), ASReturnNode (value expression), ASIdentifierNode, ASStringLiteralNode, ASNumberLiteralNode, ASArrayLiteralNode, ASDictionaryLiteralNode, ASNilLiteralNode, ASBoolLiteralNode. All nodes should inherit from a common ASASTNode base class. All public methods must have /// DocC comments. Create corresponding test files in AppScriptTests/.

title: NSException instead of abort() for AppScript runtime errors
description: Replace the abort() call in reportError:node:context: with [NSException raise:...] carrying a userInfo dict with structured error info (message, path, line, column, AppScript backtrace). This allows test code to catch and inspect errors without crashing the test runner, and enables future structured error handling. Downside: exceptions are catchable and could mask errors, so consider safeguards.
close_reason: NSException raise with userInfo implemented; all 5 error codes covered by new tests; all tests pass

title: Fix nil-URL crash in ASTestRunner when .expected file is missing
description: ASTestRunner.appscript calls [expectedURL as_stringContents] before checking whether URLForResource:withExtension: returned nil. When a test class has no companion .expected file, the URL is nil (ASNull in AppScript), and [ASNull as_stringContents] aborts the harness. Fix: guard against nil before calling as_stringContents, or use the existing hasContents check earlier. Also add a HOWTO.md to AppScriptHarness/Scripts/ explaining the .appscript + .expected pairing convention so future developers know both files are required.

title: Replace NSValue+AppScriptGeometry with BridgeSupport function calls
description: NSValue+AppScriptGeometry adds ObjC category methods (rectWithX:y:width:height:, zeroRect, sizeWithWidth:height:, pointWithX:y:) to work around AppScript's inability to call C struct-returning functions. Now that BridgeSupport exposes these functions (NSMakeRect, NSMakeSize, NSMakePoint, NSZeroRect), the category should be removed and all call sites updated to use the BridgeSupport equivalents instead.
close_reason: Implemented: extended ASBridgeSupportInstaller for struct constants and geometry returns, fixed ASParser for unnamed keyword parts, replaced NSValue+AppScriptGeometry with Foundation BridgeSupport loading.

title: Add bitwise logical operators to NSNumber category
description: AppScript has no bitwise operators, so bitmask operations (like NSWindowStyleMask combinations) require workarounds. Add a category on NSNumber with methods like bitwiseOr:, bitwiseAnd:, bitwiseXor:, bitwiseNot to enable natural bitmask construction in AppScript.

title: Tighten method signature resolution in sentinel IMP installation
description: ASProtocolTypeEncodingForSelector currently walks the full superclass chain when looking up protocol encodings for sentinel IMP installation. This could cause incorrect encodings to be installed when a method name coincidentally matches a protocol method on an unrelated superclass. Audit the sentinel installation paths in ASRuntimeInstaller.m (installSentinelForMethodNode:onClass: and the category loop) to ensure protocol encodings are only applied for selectors the AppScript class explicitly overrides via its own declared protocol conformances or direct ObjC superclass protocols. The runtime dispatch path (ASMethodSignatureForSelectorIMP) should remain unchanged.
close_reason: Audit complete — full-chain walk is correct; no code change needed, design intent documented in comments.

title: Support escape sequences in AppScript string literals
description: The AppScript parser strips @"..." delimiters but does not process escape sequences. So @"\n" becomes the literal two-character string backslash-n instead of a newline. The parser (ASParser.m ~line 810) needs to unescape \n, \t, \r, \\, \" etc. after stripping delimiters.
close_reason: Implemented unescapeString:atLine:column:error: in ASParser.m; all ObjC escape sequences supported; 17 new tests; all 770 tests pass

title: Improve harness table: show full test output
description: The AppScriptHarness results table still truncates multi-line output in the expected and actual columns. The previous fix attempt added word-wrap and dynamic row heights but the full content is still not visible.

title: Rewrite AppScriptHarness ObjC glue in AppScript
description: Convert AppDelegate.m and ASTestRunner.m from Objective-C to AppScript scripts. ASHarnessWindowController.m provides the UI infrastructure base class and should remain in ObjC (it uses NSMakeRect/NSMakeSize C structs and bitmask OR which AppScript doesn't support). AppDelegate and ASTestRunner are good candidates: AppDelegate just wires up the window controller on launch; ASTestRunner discovers ASTestCase subclasses via [ASRuntimeInstaller registeredClasses], runs them, reads their .expected files, and returns ASTestResult objects. This task tracks the actual conversion once the blocking language features are in place.
close_reason: ASTestRunner.m deleted and reimplemented in AppScript; AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching: moved to AppScript category. BOOL-returning method stays in ObjC. All integration tests pass.

title: Improve harness table: show full test output
description: The AppScriptHarness results table truncates multi-line output in the 'expected' and 'actual' columns (newlines are replaced with spaces, making diffs hard to read). Fix by either using multi-line table cells or a better whitespace substitution so the full output is visible.
close_reason: Multi-line cells with word wrap for expected/actual columns; row height calculated from max line count × 17pt + 8pt padding.

title: DocC catalog and articles for the AppScript framework
description: Create the DocC documentation catalog at AppScript/Documentation.docc/. The top-level AppScript.md catalog file must list all public types and link to all articles. Required articles: (1) LoadingAndRunningAppScriptFiles.md — the load->parse->install->invoke pipeline; (2) DefiningClassesAndCategories.md — how AppScript class and category definitions map to ObjC runtime registration; (3) ControlFlowAndArithmetic.md — the NSNumber/NSObject control flow and arithmetic API. Each article must use <doc:SymbolName> link syntax to reference every method and type it describes. This task may be worked on in parallel with implementation tasks but should be reviewed alongside each feature task.

value: design-phase-file-io-check: During Design phase for any feature that reads or writes files, explicitly search for existing project file-reading utilities before writing new I/O code (e.g. grep -r 'stringContents\|fileReading\|fileWriting'). Caught as defect in c2o: used NSString stringWithContentsOfFile: instead of the project's NSURL+AppScriptFileReading -as_stringContents. A 30-second grep at design time prevents an interface defect caught later in review.

gnustep-unit-tests-env: unit-tests.sh must set GNUSTEP_MAKEFILES=/Library/GNUstep/Makefiles before running 'make check', or source the GNUstep environment file. Without this, make fails silently with 'No such file or directory' for the include path, which looks like GNUstep is not installed — but it is. Never dismiss a GNUstep make failure as 'not installed' without first checking whether GNUSTEP_MAKEFILES is set.

psp-estimation-calibration: Updated shape distinction: (1) Narrowly scoped, 1-2 branches, 4-6 tests → ~20 min. (2) Narrowly scoped, 3-4 branches, 6-8 tests + simplify review → ~30 min. (3) Multi-method cross-cutting feature (≥3 modified methods, new internal class, thread-local state or similar, new public API, 7+ tests) → ~65 min. Plan shape 3 with: Planning=12, Design=3, Code=15, Compile=3, Test=20, Review=10, Postmortem=5. Confirmed by appscript-5j3: estimated 38 min, actual 69 min (1.82×). Add a fixed +9 min overhead to the Test phase for the AppScript project's full multi-suite run (xcodebuild unit + ASan + TSan + GNUstep + integration). Review estimate for cross-cutting features: 8-10 min (not 3-4 min) to account for parallel simplify-agent cycle.

building-gnustep-app-target-on-macos: Creating a GNUstep application.make target on macOS requires several non-obvious steps beyond the basic makefile variables. (1) Use per-target NEEDS_GUI variables (AppName_NEEDS_GUI = yes/no) rather than a global NEEDS_GUI. (2) Use RESOURCE_FILES_DIR + wildcard to copy script/resource files directly into Resources/ top level — RESOURCE_DIRS only creates empty directories; RESOURCE_FILES with a path creates a subdirectory; NSBundle URLsForResourcesWithExtension:subdirectory:nil only searches Resources/ top level and language subdirectories, not arbitrary subdirs. (3) Set MAIN_MODEL_FILE = MainMenu.nib to populate NSMainNibFile in Info.plist; compile the xib with ibtool in an after-AppName-all:: double-colon target (guard with xcrun --find ibtool so it skips on Linux). (4) Embed built frameworks in Contents/Frameworks/ via cp -Rf in after-all, then use install_name_tool -change to rewrite the relative framework install name to @executable_path/../Frameworks/...; add -Wl,-headerpad_max_install_names to LDFLAGS so install_name_tool has room to write longer paths. (5) Also rewrite libgnustep-baseadd's bare install name to its full /usr/local/lib/ path the same way. (6) Re-sign the binary with 'codesign --sign - --force' after all install_name_tool changes (omit --preserve-metadata=entitlements as it fails on unsigned binaries). Without re-signing, Apple Silicon will refuse to run the modified binary.

requirements-observability-check: During planning of any runtime-error or exception-handling feature, explicitly ask: 'How does a host application observe this in production (crash reports, logs, uncaught exception handler, etc.)?' The appscript-oot postmortem found that implementing the hybrid backtrace without a corresponding callable handler API left the feature incomplete — discovered only in post-task review, leading to appscript-2de as a follow-on. Make observability a standard planning checklist item for runtime features.

test-global-state-isolation: Any XCTestCase that writes to global process state (NSUncaughtExceptionHandler, signal handlers, NSNotification observers, NSUserDefaults, etc.) must save and restore that state in setUp/tearDown. Write setUp/tearDown as the FIRST thing when creating a test file that interacts with system-level APIs — before any test methods. Failure to do this was caught as a defect in appscript-2de review.

testing-untestable-paths: When a code path cannot be tested directly (e.g. it calls abort() or exit()), ask: 'Is there an observable side effect of the *other* branch I can test instead?' Pattern: install a flag-setting callback as the pre-existing handler, invoke the installed handler with a non-matching input, assert the flag was set. Generalises to any handler/callback with a fallthrough branch. Caught as missing test in appscript-2de review.

design-phase-field-liveness-check: Before finishing the Code phase for any new class, verify that every field declared on that class is actually read somewhere in the feature's code path. On appscript-5j3, ASCallFrame.receiver was written at push time but never read in ASFormatCallFrame or anywhere in the backtrace path — caught only in Review. A 30-second read of the new class's usage before finalising the Code phase would catch this. Checklist item: for each new field, grep for its name in the implementation to confirm it is read at least once.

forwardInvocation-design-checklist: When implementing forwardInvocation:-based dispatch, at Design phase explicitly enumerate every ObjC message send inside the block body. Ask: 'If this selector is also installed as a sentinel on this class by external code, what happens?' Two expensive defects on asu-2pl (48 min combined) stemmed from: (1) property accessors on blockSelf inside forwardInvocation: — use blockSelf->_ivar direct access instead; (2) class_addMethod silently installs sentinels for inherited NSObject methods (retain/release) — guard with instancesRespondToSelector: which checks the full hierarchy. Both could have been caught at design time with this checklist.

gnustep-build-additional-tips: Additional GNUstep build tips beyond the main memory. (1) ARC: Always set ADDITIONAL_OBJCFLAGS = -fobjc-arc when porting code from Xcode projects — GNUstep makefiles default to MRC but all Xcode projects use ARC. (2) Launch testing: 'make' success alone is insufficient for app targets — always launch-test the GNUstep-built binary explicitly (open AppScriptHarness.app or equivalent). The run-tests skill runs Xcode integration tests, NOT the GNUstep-built app. (3) Pre-read make sources: Before coding any GNUstep target, read the relevant $(GNUSTEP_MAKEFILES)/Instance/*.make file to understand the variables — 1 min of reading prevents hours of compile+test repair. (4) Codesigning GNUstep app bundles: GNUstep-make adds a stamp file (e.g. stamp.make) inside the .app bundle directory. codesign rejects bundles containing unexpected files, so the stamp file must be removed before running codesign. Fixed in this project by deleting the stamp file in an after-app-all:: hook before the codesign step. (5) run-tests scripts: Always verify integration-tests.sh and unit-tests.sh work end-to-end immediately after creating them — the original integration-tests.sh referenced scheme 'AppScriptHarnessUITests' which does not exist as a scheme (target exists but was never added to a named scheme; xcodebuild test requires a scheme name).

GNUstep Make reserves several top-level phony targets using double-colon rules (e.g. check::, install::, clean::) defined in $(GNUSTEP_MAKEFILES)/Master/rules.make. Custom GNUmakefiles must NOT redefine these with single-colon rules (causes 'has both : and :: entries' error). Instead, hook into the corresponding double-colon extension points: before-<target>::, internal-<target>::, or after-<target>::. Example: to add custom logic to 'make check', define 'internal-check::' rather than 'check:'. Discovered while implementing appscript-z0t. Worth writing up as generic GNUstep Make documentation for reuse across projects and by other agents.

integration-tests-always-required: Always run the integration test suite (integration-tests.sh) before declaring a task complete, not just unit tests. This is a recurring failure mode across multiple PSP tasks (ewo, xjo) — unit tests pass, integration tests skipped until user prompts. The psp-develop skill says 'ensure all tests pass including existing tests' but in practice this is forgotten. Explicit rule: after all unit tests + sanitizer runs pass, run integration-tests.sh before closing the issue. Also: when writing a new integration test, always run the harness once with a placeholder .expected file and capture actual output before committing to final .expected content (capture-then-assert pattern). The AppScriptHarness requires paired .appscript + .expected files — missing .expected causes a nil-URL crash in ASTestRunner.

objc-coding-patterns-appscript: Key ObjC patterns for this codebase. (1) NSException: NEVER use [NSException raise:format:] — it has no userInfo: parameter. Always use [NSException exceptionWithName:reason:userInfo:] then call -raise on the result. (2) noreturn methods: When calling a __attribute__((noreturn)) method, always follow the call site with __builtin_unreachable() — do not rely on Clang to infer noreturn through an ObjC message send. (3) Test helper classes: Place test-local helper classes ABOVE the test class's @interface, NOT inside @implementation. ObjC does not allow nested @interface/@implementation blocks. Match the pattern already established in test files (e.g. ASSuperTestBase/ASSuperTestSub are defined before @interface ASInterpreterTests). (4) Framework headers: Always read framework headers before editing them (e.g. AppScript.framework/Versions/0/Headers/), even if the source header was already read — they are separate files that must stay in sync.

parallel-test-isolation-smoke: For any new test class that installs global ObjC runtime state (forwardInvocation: blocks, sentinel IMPs, class method registrations), run a parallel-isolation smoke test before marking Code complete: xcodebuild -only-testing:NewTestClass -only-testing:NSBundle_AppScriptBridgeSupportLoadingTests. Catches cross-process sentinel contamination 40+ min earlier than full test suite. Lesson from asu-2pl defect 4.

psp-estimation-calibration: For ObjC runtime dispatch tasks (forwardInvocation:, imp_implementationWithBlock, class_addMethod sentinel patterns): Code phase is fast (6 min for 1400 lines across 8 files); Test phase is slow (3x overrun typical). Recommended phase distribution: Planning 15%, Design 8%, Code 8%, Compile 15%, Test 45%, Postmortem 9%. Also add +10 min overhead for AppScript parallel test suite diagnostics when a test only fails in certain worker processes.

psp-estimation-calibration: Narrowly-scoped Objective-C tasks (add one method, propagate through 1-2 call sites, 4-6 tests) consistently run at ~0.3x estimates. Three consecutive tasks (btc, isd, xjo) all came in at 0.30-0.33x. Calibrated baseline for this shape: Planning=3m, Design=1m, Code=5m, Compile=2m, Test=5m, Postmortem=3m, Total=~20 min. Apply a 3x downward calibration factor for tasks tagged 'low effort' or 'narrowly scoped'. For identified-fix-site bugs: coding phase is ~1-5 min, not 30-45 min. For build-file tasks (GNUmakefile, CMakeLists): split Research (20-30m if novel build system) vs Mechanical authoring (~1m per 10 files + 5m boilerplate) — do NOT budget a separate Test phase since compile subsumes it.
